    tsdst.tmath.norm¶

    tsdst.tmath.norm(x, p, use_expo=False)[source]¶

    Calculate a power sum, an Lp norm, or the conventional L0 count.

    Parameters:
    xnumpy.ndarray

    Values whose norm or power sum is required.

    pint

    Norm order: zero, one, or an order of at least two. Zero returns the number of nonzero entries, including negative entries.

    use_expobool, optional

    Apply the final 1/p exponent for a positive order when True. If False, return sum(abs(x)**p), as commonly used in regularization penalties. The default is False. The option does not affect the L0 count.

    Returns:
    valuenumeric

    Power sum, rooted norm, or nonzero count.

    Notes

    Ridge regularization commonly uses the squared L2 norm, so this helper omits the square root by default. L0 is the conventional sparsity count; it is not a mathematical norm because it does not satisfy homogeneity.
